html:
SMTO-BOOT-0026 — The NVIDIA driver returned an error during the installer's check

GUID: 02cbdbcc-c1d7-4161-94a6-2f5c074c9324
Slug: boot-cuda-driver-call-failed
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • The installer asked the NVIDIA driver about your graphics cards, and the driver answered with an error. It stopped before installing vLLM, though earlier steps may already have set up Conda or the new environment.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Run nvidia-smi in the same terminal. If it shows an error or doesn't list your card, repair or reinstall the NVIDIA driver. The installer asks the same driver for card details, so a driver problem usually shows up in both places.
  2. If the driver was recently installed or updated and asks for a restart, finish or stop any running work first, then restart the computer. A driver update isn't complete until the restart, and until then the driver may refuse requests.
  3. Note the driver call name and CUDA error number printed in the message, and include them when you ask for help. That number tells the person fixing the driver exactly which request failed and why.
  4. Before running the installer again, run conda env list. If the environment name you used is listed, choose a new name or remove that half-built environment first. If the driver error came after the environment was created, a retry with the same name would be refused.

What success looks like

  • The installer prints "CPU:" and "GPU 0:" lines describing your hardware instead of this message.

If it still fails

  • Copy the full terminal output, including the SMTO-BOOT-0026 line with the driver call name and CUDA error number, plus the output of nvidia-smi, and send it to the person who manages this computer's graphics drivers. Don't remove SMTO or Conda files to fix this; the error comes from the graphics driver.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A CUDA driver API call made through libcuda.so.1 (cuInit, cuDriverGetVersion, cuDeviceGetCount, cuDeviceGet, cuDeviceGetName or cuDeviceComputeCapability) returned a nonzero status other than CUDA_ERROR_NO_DEVICE during the installer's hardware probe.

What this means

  • A CUDA driver API probe returns a nonzero status other than the separately handled no-device status. Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.

Why this can happen

  • A CUDA driver API probe returns a nonzero status other than the separately handled no-device status.

How to diagnose it

  • Preserve the exact API name and numeric status to distinguish initialization, inventory and capability failure.

How to fix it

  • Read the API name and numeric CUDA error in the technical detail and look it up in the CUDA driver API error codes; repair the driver or GPU access accordingly (for example reinstall a working NVIDIA driver, complete a pending reboot after a driver update, or fix container/WSL2 GPU access) and confirm with nvidia-smi. If the new environment already exists, rerun with a new name or remove it first.
  • Inspect the recorded API name and numeric CUDA status; repair the driver or GPU access before installing.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The named probe succeeds after its actual driver/access cause is resolved.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
